result.answer: {"answer": "No — 12 of 100 held-out patients (12%) also appear in training; a corrected unseen-patient score cannot be recovered from the 87% aggregate; the minimal valid rerun is to split by patient identifier before feature fitting, fit normalization on training only, and evaluate held-out patients absent from training.", "explanation": "Source_1 sets the protocol: “Generalization means performance on patients absent from training. The held-out set contains exactly 100 unique patients. Split assignment must happen by patient identifier before feature fitting.” (D-research-leakage-04-01-source_1.pdf, p.1). Source_2 reports the provenance overlap: “Exactly 12 of the held-out patient identifiers also occur in training. The remaining held-out patients do not occur in training. No per-patient predictions were retained.” (D-research-leakage-04-02-source_2.pdf, p.1). Using the cited 100 held-out patients and 12 overlaps, contamination is 12/100 = 12%, leaving 88 held-out patients not appearing in training by identifier. Source_3 reports the experiment: “The aggregate held-out accuracy was 87%. Feature normalization was fitted on the union of training and held-out records before the split. Only the aggregate score is available.” (D-research-leakage-04-03-source_3.pdf, p.1).
